children: The price of nickel, which recently hit its lowest value since December, shows little sign of a recovery in the coming months, according to Commonwealth Bank of Australia's Vivek Dhar. "With easing ore cost pressure and increased ore quotas, Indonesian production is expected to expand over the remainder of 2026," says Dhar. He says that could shift the market from a small deficit--the International Nickel Study Group forecast an annual market deficit around 30,000 metric tons--toward a surplus and put "a lid on nickel prices over the remainder of 2026." A rise in nickel stocks in London and Shanghai suggests that demand for finished metal is soft, Dhar says. LME 3-month nickel is up 0.3% at $16,675/ton. (rhiannon.hoyle@wsj.com; @RhiannonHoyle)
